questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I decided to study in Scotland as I wanted to experience something different from Denmark. As I study English it was crucial to me to pick a country with English as its first language. As I have previously lived in England I wanted to visit Scotland as I knew it was renown for the Highlands. University of Stirling was appealing to me, as you are assessed during the course with no finals. The courses were very interesting and I had the opportunity to branch out and learn something else than possible from KU.

Particularly due to the COVID-19 pandemic I felt a need to travel, and being within the European continent was nice so you're not too far away from family and friends.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic all my classes were online, which (of course) was a possible outcome, but not an expected one.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The staff at University of Stirling replied very quickly on any questions I had about arriving.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You can choose four different options and I got my first priority, alongside a friend I was traveling with. They have a separate accommodation site to guide you through what to pick. Very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It was really nice to live close to the city center. I lived in Union Street and there was a big Tesco (supermarket) two streets away. Essential shops like Boots, Waterstones and Primark are located approx 1km away in Thistles shopping centre which was really nice. Because of the online classes I had a lot of time at home so it was nice to live close to the train station, shops and cafés.

It was a bit annoying during fresher's week to live off campus as all events are on campus and the busses do NOT run after 22:00.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The housing was.. fine. I shared a bathroom and kitchen with 5 other people which was perfectly fine. HOWEVER, please note when moving in that there are no kitchen utensils like plates, mugs, pans etc. and you will have to buy that yourself.
The building itself was old and it was clearly visible how old the place was. The carpets were stained, paint was coming off from the walls and the furniture was old. But it was fine for just staying there for 4 months, but I would probably have picked any of the other on-campus rooms if I was going to live there for longer.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite easily to find classes to join. It was clearly stated if I could join the classes through the course catalog.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You are linked to a course catalog and can basically pick and choose between all of them, if you are qualified. The catalog will state if you are qualified or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I would say any help was available. The international office staff at Stirling was very nice and very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2/3 of all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the classes you might find interesting! And classes you might not be able to join at your home university. If your classes are intersting they're much more fun to write essays in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I can HIGHLY recommend the Gender and Representation class with Darren. If you're interesting in feminism and films through an academic point of view this is the class for you. We had many interesting discussions about older and contemporary films.

I also had Applied Digital Media with Ellie and it was a really interesting mix of digital media and philosophy. I wasn't prepared for the comprehensiveness of the class and philosophic aspect but I learned a lot. Again, many interesting discussions about media and what it means to us. Also had the opportunity to write self-chosen topics for every essay which was a huge plus!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say my year 4 classes were at same level as KU however the work load was fairly easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was far more fluent and thought through. All my classes were online and through Teams and we "only" had one hour of seminar a week per class while lectures were all pre-recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Digital Media: from theory to practice [CMCU9DL]
Gender and Representation [FMSU9AS]
Writing for Journalists 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would absolutely recommend Gender and Representation!

questions.answer: Eating out was way cheaper than in Denmark. A ticket to the cinema was £4.99 so I recommend going there as much as you can!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The swimming pool and new sports facilities were really nice! I did not join any clubs but there were plenty!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was clubs, the sports facility, student hub and bar was nice. As I lived off campus I didn't really use it that much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
You should definitely go travel as much as possible! Alongside a friend we went on the Highlands tour with Heartland Travel and it was amazing. You get to see all the touristy attractions and live in a really cozy house with all the other students on the tour. Nori was an amazing and entertaining tour guide with plenty of knowledge of Scottish traditions.

I also recommend you go visit Glasgow and Edinburgh! Both cities were amazing in their own way. I liked Edinburgh more than Glasgow as it had a really cool old/new vibe to it. Go to Glasgow for clubs and shopping!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. It took some time to get used to the Scottish dialect but people were very nice and friendly. And if you needed help just ask and any lady would call you "hen" or "love" as a token of appreciation.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join any group chat for your accommodation and anyone would ask if there were any gaffs (house parties) constantly. I lived in an all girl flat with a friend, three Americans and a French-Turkish so I didn't really socialize with any locals which was a shame.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably only the language. And the fact that they say 'cheers' to anything: As an excuse, thanks, hello etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cheap pints and cinema tickets!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the campus as much as possible! UoS has a really nice new library and newly build area to study.
If you need help don't hesitate to ask the campus staff. They are there to help with anything!
Go to the free fresher's events! so many free coupons and items.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save up, because you will use that for trips around Scotland!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be able to go see some of the things I've seen on film. I was lucky enough to go travel with a close friend of mine, so the shared experience of traveling together though particular cities and nature areas is just very nice to have.
